title: The Sunny Spot Rota
logline: Pip and Nimbus both want the one warm sunny spot on the hill — Pip for his reading corner, Nimbus for a nap. Each keeps politely ceding it, then sneaking back, until politeness itself becomes the competition.
starting_goal: Both want to enjoy the single sunny spot on the hill
friction_source: One spot, two desires; each wants the other to have it AND wants it himself
character_want: Both: belonging — each wants the other to be happy but fears giving up his own comfort entirely
power_usage: None; Nimbus's shadow over the spot is his body, not a power use
escalation: Politeness escalates by kind: ceding -> scheduling -> an elaborate flag-and-timetable system nobody enjoys
emotional_beat: Each admits he wanted to share the spot, not own it — they sit squeezed together, slightly squashed, happy
rewatch_detail: The timetable board in the background fills with increasingly tiny handwriting across scenes
distinctness_note: Conflict is mutual generosity, not an accident; no object breaks and no weather matters

title: One Rain, Two Thirsts
logline: Nimbus has only one small rain in him today. The garden bed is thirsty and the paper boat needs a puddle. Whoever he helps, he must disappoint someone — maybe himself.
starting_goal: Nimbus wants to help both the garden and the boat game with his single available rain
friction_source: A bounded resource (one mild rain, per the cost rule) against two legitimate needs
character_want: Nimbus: needed — helping is his bid for belonging, so choosing who not to help feels like choosing who not to love
power_usage: One bounded mild rain is the scarce resource; a watering can would keep the story but lose the body-cost legibility
escalation: Nimbus tries micro-drizzles for both, going grey and saggy; the drip-trickle satisfies nobody and worries everybody
emotional_beat: Pip reroutes the stream so one rain serves both — and Nimbus learns being needed includes being protected from himself
rewatch_detail: The snail appears in the background of every scene slowly approaching the garden, foreshadowing the reframe
distinctness_note: The scarcity is the character's own bounded capacity, making the power philosophy's cost rule the plot engine

title: The Snail's Favorite
logline: A visiting snail seems to prefer Pip's lettuce to Nimbus's soft mist. Nimbus escalates his offerings; the snail, unimpressed, heads for the one thing neither offered.
starting_goal: Both want to welcome the visiting snail well
friction_source: Perceived preference of a care-receiver triggers comparison
character_want: Nimbus: needed — being second-choice at caretaking threatens his whole belonging strategy
power_usage: Nimbus's mist/drizzle offerings get fancier in pattern (not in kind or power) as he competes
escalation: Offerings escalate by kind: mist -> drizzle pattern -> an apologetic little personal rainbow of droplets that mostly soaks Nimbus
emotional_beat: The snail settles in the dry shade between them — it never wanted offerings, just company; Nimbus laughs in a gust of relief
rewatch_detail: The snail's slime trail quietly spells its route toward the shade from scene one onward
distinctness_note: Jealousy resolved by observing what the care-receiver actually wants, not by winning the competition

title: The Tower and the Wind That Cheered
logline: Pebble-stacking contest: Pip's engineered tower versus Nimbus's wobbly stack. Every time Nimbus gets excited about his own stack, his gust-knocks it down himself.
starting_goal: Both want to win a friendly pebble-stacking contest
friction_source: Nimbus's excitement physically undermines his own effort (expressive leak)
character_want: Nimbus: needed/wanted — winning would prove he is good at something; excitement about possibly winning is what defeats him
power_usage: Excited skittery gusts from Nimbus topple only his own stacks; mild, self-directed, no danger
escalation: Escalation by kind: steady breathing tricks -> Pip coaching stillness -> Nimbus holding his breath until he wobbles and both collapse laughing
emotional_beat: Nimbus stops trying not to be excited and builds a stack designed to dance in his gusts — they build one shared wind-proof wall instead
rewatch_detail: Pip's tower gains one pebble in the background every time Nimbus fails — quiet scoreboard
distinctness_note: Self-defeating excitement: the power leak sabotages the self, not the friend or an object

title: The Regatta of Overengineering
logline: Paper boat race down the stream. Pip spends so long perfecting his boat that he misses most of the race; Nimbus's lopsided boat, cheered on by its maker, is undone by the cheering itself.
starting_goal: Both want their paper boat to win the stream race
friction_source: Opposite failure styles: Pip's excess preparation, Nimbus's leaky enthusiasm
character_want: Pip: wanted — winning with a perfect plan would prove his worth; Nimbus: needed — a cheered-on boat is a loved boat
power_usage: Nimbus's cheering gusts accidentally push Pip's boat backward; the leak raises but does not carry the story
escalation: Pip adds ballast, then a rudder, then a flag system while boats finish without him; Nimbus cheers so hard his own boat spins
emotional_beat: A plain leaf wins the race; both laugh and cheer for the leaf together — shared defeat tastes better than solo victory
rewatch_detail: The leaf that wins is visible caught on a reed in the opening shot; freed by the world's breeze at the start
distinctness_note: Neither flaw is corrected; the world simply declines to reward either strategy, and friendship gets the win

title: The Quiet Game
logline: Who can stay quiet longest? Nimbus is winning until a suppressed giggle escapes as a tiny gust that tickles Pip. Pip retaliates with faces. Both are doomed.
starting_goal: Both try to win the staying-quiet game
friction_source: Suppressing laughter makes it physically leak (suppression backfire)
character_want: Nimbus: wanted — winning the game would make him fun company; the wanting is what leaks
power_usage: Suppressed giggles escape as small tickling gusts; the comedy depends entirely on the leak mechanic
escalation: Escalation by kind: held breath -> strategic yawning -> Pip's outrageous faces -> Nimbus inflating like a balloon to hold it in
emotional_beat: Both burst at once; the snail, motionless, is declared the eternal champion and they bring it a leaf as a trophy
rewatch_detail: The snail doesn't move the entire episode — the longest quiet-game player visible from the start
distinctness_note: Pure character comedy with zero plot machinery; tests whether E2 suppression-backfire can carry a whole episode

title: The Hill That Answers Everyone
logline: Pip discovers the echoing hill answers him and spends happy mornings trading calls. Nimbus, feeling replaced, drizzles on the hill to join the game — and muffles the echo he wanted to be part of.
starting_goal: Nimbus wants to share the new echo game Pip loves
friction_source: Fear of being replaced leads to an action that damages the thing he wants to join
character_want: Nimbus: needed — Pip has a new friend that needs nothing from Nimbus
power_usage: Jealous drizzle muffles the echo; any dampening would work, but the leak makes it involuntary and confessional
escalation: Nimbus's attempts to join escalate by kind: hovering closer -> drizzle -> trying to BE the echo with gust-voice, which scatters his own droplets
emotional_beat: The hill answers everyone — even the snail's slow slide gets a soft return; being one of many doesn't shrink Pip's calls
rewatch_detail: The echo repeats Nimbus's first tiny worried hum back to him in every early scene, unnoticed
distinctness_note: Jealousy aimed at a non-person world feature; the resolution teaches inclusivity of affection, not apology for feeling

title: The Suggestion Box
logline: Everyone leaves Pip plan-requests at the notice board. Nimbus builds a suggestion box for himself; every note asks for weather. He didn't want to be useful — he wanted to be wanted.
starting_goal: Nimbus wants to receive requests like Pip does
friction_source: The community values his function, not his company — his deepest fear delivered by mail
character_want: Nimbus: needed vs wanted — being asked only for rain confirms 'I am a tool'
power_usage: None on screen; the episode is about the power's social meaning, not its use
escalation: Nimbus performs his box duties with increasing ceremony and decreasing joy; the final note requests something no cloud can do: his company at the picnic
emotional_beat: The last note — 'please come sit with us, no rain needed' — lands; Nimbus's happy mist rains upward, briefly
rewatch_detail: Sharp-eyed viewers can read one pinned background note early: a drawing of Nimbus with hearts that he never notices
distinctness_note: The power becomes the emotional problem rather than the tool; direct test of the wanted-vs-needed axis

title: The Perfect Planter Nobody Saw
logline: Everyone admires Nimbus's rain over the garden. Pip's beautiful planter stands unnoticed. Pip insists he doesn't mind. His tidying says otherwise.
starting_goal: Pip wants his careful work to be noticed; will not admit it
friction_source: Pip's belonging bid (competence) loses the attention contest to Nimbus's flashier one
character_want: Pip: wanted — being overlooked for the thing he is proudest of confirms 'boring'
power_usage: None; Nimbus must read Pip WITHOUT any weather tell — the reverse-reading test
escalation: Pip's denial escalates by kind: re-tidying the planter -> 'accidentally' placing it center-path -> a label, then a bigger label, then a small signpost system
emotional_beat: Nimbus learns Pip's tell (the too-neat stack) and waters the planter so it blooms — noticed at last, Pip pretends it was the plan; Nimbus lets him
rewatch_detail: Pip's planter migrates toward the center of the frame across scenes before anyone comments
distinctness_note: Proves Pip's emotional engine works with zero weather; the reader/read relationship reverses direction

title: The Personal Rain That Followed Him
logline: Nimbus trips at the muffin-stall pickup — nothing broken, dignity dented. An apologetic drizzle starts following him around. The harder he pretends it isn't happening, the harder it drizzles.
starting_goal: Nimbus wants to finish the muffin pickup as if nothing happened
friction_source: Embarrassment manifests as a following drizzle; denial feeds it
character_want: Nimbus: not a burden — a public stumble plus visible feelings is his nightmare twice over
power_usage: Embarrassment drizzle tracks Nimbus and intensifies with denial; core mechanic is the expressive power philosophy
escalation: Escalation by kind: angled hovering to dodge his own rain -> a hat (it rains inside the hat) -> standing in the stream 'on purpose'
emotional_beat: Pip silently holds an umbrella over himself too, so Nimbus isn't the only one under one; Nimbus's drizzle turns warm and stops
rewatch_detail: The muffin-stall queue's shadow line shifts as everyone quietly edges to make room for one small raining cloud
distinctness_note: The weather IS the emotion and the plot; strongest single test of the expressive-power hypothesis

title: The Rehearsed Wave
logline: Pip rehearses the perfect thank-you wave for the anonymous muffin-baker who leaves notes. At the real moment he blanks, does all nine rehearsals at once, and his plan-cards scatter.
starting_goal: Pip wants to thank the muffin-baker gracefully
friction_source: Preparation cannot survive contact with a live moment
character_want: Pip: wanted — the perfect gesture would make him memorable, not boring
power_usage: A sympathetic gust from Nimbus scatters the plan-cards, revealing them; removable but it forces the confession
escalation: Rehearsal escalates by kind: wave variants -> cue cards -> choreographed turn-and-wave with marks on the ground
emotional_beat: The scattered cards ARE the thank-you — the baker's next note praises 'the funny little card dance'; Pip frames the note and hides the frame
rewatch_detail: Each rehearsal number (1-9) is visible on a card; the final accidental performance clearly runs through all nine in order
distinctness_note: Embarrassment where the failed performance becomes the appreciated artifact; the plan's failure is the gift

title: The Berry Map
logline: Pip knocks over the stacked berry baskets and hides the juice stain on his map by renaming it a 'berry route'. Nimbus's helpful washing drizzle makes the stain — and the lie — impossible to miss.
starting_goal: Pip wants to deliver the berry baskets without anyone knowing he spilled them
friction_source: A hidden mistake plus a friend whose help cannot be steered away from it
character_want: Pip: competent-wanted — the spill threatens the only identity he trusts
power_usage: Nimbus's washing drizzle spreads the stain; water could come from the stream, but his unsteerable eagerness is the joke
escalation: Concealment escalates by kind: folded map corner -> decoy 'berry route' -> re-drawing the whole map at night, stain included, in official ink
emotional_beat: Pip confesses to the basket-owner note; reply note: the 'berry route' marks a patch nobody knew — the stain stays on the official map
rewatch_detail: The stain's shape slowly resembles a berry more with each scene, ending as the map's official berry symbol
distinctness_note: Pip as mistake-hider (not Nimbus) with Nimbus as innocence-driven exposer; competence hierarchy inverted

title: Cloud-Light Lemonade
logline: The stall expects the pair's famous lemonade. Nimbus's worry about disappointing everyone drips into the pitcher all morning — the lemonade gets lighter and lighter until it isn't lemonade.
starting_goal: Deliver the promised lemonade to the stall on time
friction_source: Promise deadline versus worry that physically dilutes the product
character_want: Nimbus: needed — being trusted with the stall's order is the belonging he craves, and the craving ruins the order
power_usage: Worry-drip dilutes the pitcher progressively; the mechanism requires the expressive leak
escalation: Escalation by kind: taste-tests that get quieter -> secret re-squeezing -> a 'concentrate' plan that requires hiding the pitcher from its own maker
emotional_beat: They tell the stall the truth; the queue votes 'cloud-light' the best batch ever — honesty, relabeled as a recipe
rewatch_detail: The pitcher's level rises as its color fades across scenes; the snail refuses the first sample and accepts the last
distinctness_note: Social pressure literally enters the product; honesty-as-resolution rather than honesty-as-lesson

title: The Kite Trick That Grew
logline: Nimbus mentioned one kite loop; by note-retelling it has become a flying show. The queue gathers. The trick he never actually promised is now expected.
starting_goal: Nimbus wants to live up to the exaggerated show everyone expects
friction_source: Reputation inflation he did not create but is too pleased to correct
character_want: Nimbus: wanted — the crowd's excitement is the belonging drug; correcting it means deflating it
power_usage: Kite wind must come from Nimbus; forced, nervous gusts behave worse than natural ones (sincerity-keyed expression)
escalation: Escalation by kind: rehearsed loop -> wobble -> an improvised crash-dodge that LOOKS like a trick and gets the biggest cheer
emotional_beat: Nimbus lands the kite and shows everyone the wobble on purpose; the honest wobble becomes the requested finale
rewatch_detail: The notice-board drawing of the trick gains extra loops in each background appearance as the rumor grows
distinctness_note: Tests sincerity-keyed power expression under social pressure; failure-then-honesty structure instead of success

title: The Tidy-Path Inspection
logline: The community's tidy-path day is coming. Pip perfects the path; Nimbus grows quieter — his natural way is to leave little puddle-prints everywhere. Pip must choose between the perfect path and the welcome friend.
starting_goal: Pip wants the path to pass tidy-path day
friction_source: A community standard collides with a friend's nature
character_want: Pip: competent-wanted versus loyal — the plan that excludes Nimbus succeeds and feels like failure
power_usage: Puddle-prints are Nimbus's nature, not a power use; no weather is deployed
escalation: Perfectionism escalates by kind: raked gravel -> geometric pebble edging -> a 'no hovering' rule Nimbus obeys by holding painfully still above the path
emotional_beat: Pip designates one official Wild Corner; the inspection note singles it out as the best part — belonging, formalized
rewatch_detail: The Wild Corner's sign starts as a tiny chalk scribble and gains an official frame by the end
distinctness_note: Social expectation resolved by changing the standard, not the friend; no weather involved at all

title: Two Invitations, One Afternoon
logline: The garden bed needs watering and the stream regatta starts at the same hour. Both friends want to do both. Splitting up fails; doing both half-heartedly fails worse.
starting_goal: Fulfill the watering favor and attend the regatta
friction_source: Two legitimate community requests with the same deadline
character_want: Both: needed by the community — declining either feels like declining a friend
power_usage: Rain could water the garden faster, but speed was never the problem — choosing was
escalation: Escalation by kind: synchronized hurry -> each secretly abandoning their post to check on the other -> both arriving at the regatta carrying watering cans
emotional_beat: They choose the garden together and miss the race; a regatta leaf-boat drifts home to them anyway, and they hold a two-boat race at dusk
rewatch_detail: The sun's position tracks the real time pressure across scenes; the missed regatta's ribbon blows past the garden unnoticed mid-episode
distinctness_note: Neither option is wrong; the lesson-free cost of choosing is the actual story

title: The Unsayable News
logline: The kite festival is cancelled. Pip knows. Nimbus is already polishing the kite. Every route Pip plans to break the news gently makes the moment worse.
starting_goal: Pip wants to tell Nimbus the festival is cancelled without crushing him
friction_source: Honesty versus protection: every planned soft-landing is a small lie
character_want: Pip: wanted as the good-news friend; fears being the rain on the parade himself
power_usage: None; Nimbus's visible rising excitement is acting, not power use
escalation: Escalation by kind: choreographed casual mention -> a decoy 'smaller festival' -> a full fake agenda that Nimbus finds delightful, making confession harder
emotional_beat: Nimbus sees the cancelled notice himself, sees the fake agenda, and understands both at once — he pretends to love the fake plan long enough for them to laugh
rewatch_detail: Nimbus's kite gets shinier each scene (more polish = more visible excitement) while Pip's notes get smaller
distinctness_note: Pip's flaw (planning feelings) aimed at protecting rather than winning; kindness as the thing that backfires

title: Half a Cloud
logline: The garden needs rain and the laundry line needs wind — both now. Nimbus tries to drizzle and blow at once and ends up grey, saggy, and half of each.
starting_goal: Nimbus wants to answer both requests at once
friction_source: One body, two simultaneous duties; his capacity is the scarce resource
character_want: Nimbus: needed by both — refusing either feels like refusing love
power_usage: Simultaneous drizzle-plus-gust exhausts him (visible grey sag = cost made physical); the bound IS the plot
escalation: Escalation by kind: alternating fast -> both at once -> splitting attention so finely that the drizzle lands on the laundry and the wind waters the garden
emotional_beat: Pip asks the garden which matters more; the snail's trail points to the garden bed; the laundry simply waits until morning, and nothing bad happens
rewatch_detail: The laundry flaps in progressively slower rhythm as the world's natural breeze dies — a quiet clock
distinctness_note: Bounded capacity as explicit story physics; tests the cost rule of the power philosophy as drama

title: The Branch and the Forecast
logline: A fallen branch blocks the path. Pip's rigging plan needs a push at exactly the right second; Nimbus's gusts come when his confidence does. Pip must learn to read the gust before it arrives.
starting_goal: Move the fallen branch off the path together
friction_source: Nimbus's wind is sincerity-keyed; timing the plan means reading the friend
character_want: Both: needed — the task is impossible alone, and each holds half the skill
power_usage: Nimbus's gusts vary with his confidence; Pip's plan works only when he reads the emotional forecast correctly
escalation: Escalation by kind: gust too early -> gust too late -> gust perfect but Pip looking the wrong way; confidence wobble after each miss makes the next gust stranger
emotional_beat: Pip stops watching the branch and watches Nimbus instead; the gust comes; the branch rolls; Nimbus was strongest when seen, not measured
rewatch_detail: The audience can see Nimbus's confidence swell physically a beat before each gust — the forecast-irony mechanic at its purest
distinctness_note: The signature hypothesis episode: reading a friend's state IS the engineering solution

title: The Picnic and the Ordinary Breeze
logline: The world's own mild breeze keeps taking the picnic napkins. Pip's weights fail, Nimbus's counter-gusts fail; the answer is to stop fighting the breeze and lay the picnic with it.
starting_goal: Lay a picnic that survives the natural breeze
friction_source: An environmental force neither controls; Nimbus is NOT the weather this time
character_want: Both: competent-wanted — the failure stings precisely because weather is 'their thing'
power_usage: Counter-gusts fail (mild vs mild, and the world is free while Nimbus tires); the story stands with any failed fixes
escalation: Escalation by kind: pebble weights -> counter-gusts -> an elaborate napkin tether web that launches everything at once when one knot slips
emotional_beat: They move the picnic into the breeze's lane and let napkins become kites; lunch tastes better downwind
rewatch_detail: The breeze's direction is readable from the stream's ripples in every scene — an observant viewer can predict each napkin escape
distinctness_note: The world owns the weather for once; the cloud character holds no advantage, testing whether the duo works as underdogs of nature

title: Spontaneity, Scheduled
logline: For one day they swap jobs: Nimbus plans, Pip improvises. Pip writes 'be spontaneous' into a schedule. Nimbus's plan is one word: 'float'. Both are terrible; both are glorious.
starting_goal: Each wants to prove the other's way is doable
friction_source: Role reversal against nature; each respects the other's job only by failing at it
character_want: Both: wanted for themselves, not their function — each fears being only a method
power_usage: Nimbus's 'float plan' drifts with real breezes; any drift works, his just has better comic timing
escalation: Escalation by kind: Pip's spontaneity has phases -> phases get sub-steps -> his improv alarm rings during Nimbus's one-item plan review
emotional_beat: Each begs to stop pretending; the honest relief is the funniest moment of the day, and both claim the other won
rewatch_detail: Pip's schedule card visibly loses formatting discipline scene by scene until it's one crayon scribble
distinctness_note: Pure engine test: comedy from identity, zero external problem

title: The Secret Wish Event
logline: Nimbus confesses a secret wish: to see his drizzle make someone smile. Pip plans an elaborate reveal event with a stage and a queue — everything except simply letting a hot day happen.
starting_goal: Pip wants to make Nimbus's secret wish come true
friction_source: Over-producing a simple wish suffocates it
character_want: Pip: needed — delivering the wish perfectly would prove his friendship is load-bearing
power_usage: The wish is about Nimbus's drizzle itself; the payoff is his own spontaneous, unplanned rain
escalation: Escalation by kind: invite list -> stage marks -> rehearsal where Nimbus's staged drizzle comes out grey and shy because staged feelings don't work (sincerity-keyed)
emotional_beat: The event collapses; the queue stays for the shade anyway; Nimbus's relieved laugh-drizzle cools everyone — the wish grants itself, unplanned
rewatch_detail: The queue's fanning hands speed up across scenes as the day warms — the real need was visible from the start
distinctness_note: The power philosophy's sincerity rule defeats the plan; the wish is granted by honesty, not effort

title: The Tidiest Side
logline: Competitive tidying: whose half of the shared shelf is neater. Pip labels; Nimbus piles 'cloudy cushions'. The cushions deflate. The labels multiply. The shelf gives up.
starting_goal: Each wants the neater shelf half
friction_source: Two incompatible definitions of 'neat'
character_want: Both: wanted — neatness is Pip's competence bid and Nimbus's imitation of it
power_usage: Nimbus's puffy cushion-piles sag with his mood; the physical comedy needs his body but no power deployment
escalation: Escalation by kind: aligned edges -> sub-categories -> Pip alphabetizes the labels; Nimbus's piles achieve load-bearing status
emotional_beat: The shelf collapses without damage and they build one shared system — Pip's labels, Nimbus's piles, one rule: things you love stay reachable
rewatch_detail: The snail's shell gets accidentally labeled 'S' mid-episode and wears the label to the end
distinctness_note: Competition over a domestic standard; resolved by inventing a third system rather than a winner

title: Look at Me, Not the Kite
logline: Pip is wholly absorbed flying the kite. Nimbus's envy gusts snarl the line — and his shame drizzle spots the kite. He didn't mean either. He meant: look at me.
starting_goal: Nimbus wants Pip's attention back from the kite
friction_source: Jealousy leaks as weather that damages the rival object, then shame leaks too
character_want: Nimbus: wanted — attention is the currency; the kite is winning it unfairly (it isn't)
power_usage: Envy-gusts snarl the kite; shame-drizzle spots it; the double leak is the whole confessional
escalation: Escalation by kind: hovering into Pip's eyeline -> 'accidental' shade over the kite -> the snarl, then the telltale shame-spots that expose the first act
emotional_beat: The sentence 'I wanted you to look at me' costs Nimbus a grey sag; Pip ties the kite to the fence and flies nothing but Nimbus for the rest of the afternoon
rewatch_detail: The kite's tail is the ribbon from PN-1027's fence — the world remembers (cross-premise callback candidate)
distinctness_note: Jealousy confessed by the body twice (act then shame); the object is incidental — the relationship is the stakes

title: Who Took the Blame
logline: A world-gust scrambles Pip's labeled leaf display just as Nimbus arrives late. Everyone assumes the cloud did it. Nimbus lets them — to spare Pip the mess-up. Pip cannot bear being spared.
starting_goal: The leaf display must face the community after the scramble
friction_source: A kind lie (taking the blame) corrodes the person it protects
character_want: Pip: wanted for the truth of him, not a protected fiction; Nimbus: needed, even as a shield
power_usage: The scrambling gust is the world's; Nimbus uses no power at all
escalation: Escalation by kind: Nimbus's apologetic re-stack (wrong species order) -> Pip over-correcting the restack at midnight -> both pretending the other's version is right
emotional_beat: Pip confesses to the community board; the reply note says the mixed leaves were more interesting — and names the real culprit: 'that breeze again'
rewatch_detail: The world's gust is forecast in scene one by the laundry line snapping once — fair callback for rewatchers
distinctness_note: Blame transfer as a kindness that hurts; both leads protect each other asymmetrically

title: Rain on Schedule
logline: The board asks Nimbus to rain for the garden every morning at nine. Scheduled rain comes out wrong — thin, grey, apologetic. His rain only works when he means it.
starting_goal: Deliver scheduled daily rain for the garden bed
friction_source: Sincerity-keyed powers versus an obligation calendar
character_want: Nimbus: needed — the scheduled trust is everything he wanted; performing it kills the thing they wanted
power_usage: The premise IS the sincerity rule: forced mild rain underperforms felt mild rain; no other object or event drives the plot
escalation: Escalation by kind: alarm-based rain -> psyching-up rituals that fool nobody, least of all the drooping seedlings -> secretly pre-feeling joy with Pip's joke cards before nine
emotional_beat: They ask the board for 'rain when the garden asks' instead; the seedlings perk at the first unscheduled, meant rain
rewatch_detail: The seedlings' posture is the episode's honest scoreboard across scenes
distinctness_note: Direct dramatic test of the expressive power philosophy's sincerity axiom under obligation

title: The Ribbon on the Fence
logline: Nimbus finds a beautiful ribbon snagged on the fence. Finders-keepers feels wrong; the note board feels far. He wears it one afternoon — and his guilt spots it with drizzle.
starting_goal: Nimbus must decide what to do with a found ribbon
friction_source: Desire versus duty, with his own body as the confession
character_want: Nimbus: wanted — the ribbon is admiration you can wear; returning it means giving admiration back
power_usage: Guilt-drizzle spots only the ribbon, never him — the leak locates the lie; any dampening works, his is funnier
escalation: Escalation by kind: wearing it 'just once' -> 'just for the walk' -> washing the guilt-spots off the ribbon nightly so he can keep it clean enough to keep
emotional_beat: He pins it to the board; the owner's note replies: 'it looked better on the cloud — keep it'; he keeps it, spotless, because now it was given
rewatch_detail: The guilt-spots form a polka pattern that matches the ribbon's own dots — visible only on close rewatch
distinctness_note: A keep-vs-return dilemma where the body prosecutes; honesty rewarded by gift, not by loss

title: Two Gifts, One Plank
logline: Each secretly builds the other a gift. Each needs the one good plank. Each quietly gives it up to the other. Both gifts end up made of scraps — and unbreakable.
starting_goal: Each wants to finish a secret gift for the other
friction_source: One resource, two secret generous plans
character_want: Both: needed — the gift is a belonging bid; the secrecy forbids coordinating the bid
power_usage: None
escalation: Escalation by kind: the plank migrates between two hidden workshops, each leaving it for the other -> each assumes the other stole it, forgives instantly, steals it back kindly -> both build with scraps and hide the shortage
emotional_beat: The gifts are exchanged: a scrap-wood rain gauge for Nimbus, a scrap-wood plan-easel for Pip; the plank sits between them, unclaimed, doing nothing, meaning everything
rewatch_detail: The plank changes location in the background of every scene; tracking it is the whole second-viewing game
distinctness_note: Mutual secret sacrifice with zero antagonist and zero weather; E4 bid collision at its purest

title: The Staring Contest
logline: Staring contest. Pip's strategy is professional boredom. Nimbus's weapon is the laugh-gust he cannot stop swallowing. The snail referees, badly.
starting_goal: Win the staring contest
friction_source: Pip's discipline versus Nimbus's unbottleable joy
character_want: Both: wanted — winning is proof of being the fun one (Nimbus) or the master of self (Pip)
power_usage: Swallowed laugh-gusts make Nimbus tremble and inflate; physics of suppression could be any trembling, his is legible weather
escalation: Escalation by kind: stillness -> provocation faces -> the snail slowly crossing the eyeline as an unwitting distraction weapon
emotional_beat: Both break at the same blink; they declare the never-blinking snail the winner and crown it with a leaf
rewatch_detail: The snail's eye-stalks never waver the entire episode — the true champion hidden in plain sight
distinctness_note: A contest with no object, no weather target, and no stakes except joy; pure two-body comedy

title: The Valley That Sang Back
logline: Nimbus privately practices a hum at the echoing hill. The hill teaches it to the valley. Now everyone is humming his private song, and he wants the ground to open.
starting_goal: Nimbus wants his practice song to stay private
friction_source: The responsive world broadcasts what he hid; suppression amplifies the broadcast
character_want: Nimbus: wanted but on his own terms — admiration without exposure
power_usage: Flustered gusts carry the hum FARTHER; the leak worsens the exposure he is trying to stop
escalation: Escalation by kind: humming quieter (the hill still hears) -> chasing the echo with gusts (echoes multiply) -> hiding under the laundry line (the sheets pick up the tune as flags of sound)
emotional_beat: From offscreen, someone hums the song back, kindly, with a new second part; Nimbus answers; the duet is the episode's only dialogue-free conversation
rewatch_detail: Each background character-sound (stream babble, laundry snap) is in the same key as the hum — the valley was always musical
distinctness_note: Embarrassment resolved by joining the exposure rather than ending it; world as amplifier, not villain
